The Compliance Blindspot

Why spreadsheets and calendar alerts are failing General Contractors

When a jobsite accident happens or your commercial carrier performs their annual audit, finding out a subcontractor had an expired policy or missing endorsement is already too late.

The Multi-Tab Excel Trap

Office staff manually log expiration dates into a spreadsheet. But spreadsheets cannot read whether the actual CG 20 10 (Ongoing Operations) or CG 20 37 (Completed Operations) forms were attached to the PDF.

Leaves GC personally liable in injury lawsuits

The Broker Phone-Tag Cycle

When policies lapse, office staff waste 2 hours drafting emails and calling 40 different commercial brokers. Brokers ignore generic requests because project requirements aren't explicitly detailed.

10–15 hours/week of wasted administrative labor

Enterprise Software Extortion

Tools like myCOI and Procore charge $5,000–$10,000/year, require mandatory 60-minute sales demos, enforce minimum vendor quotas, and take months to onboard.

Unjustified overhead for mid-market builders

Frequently Asked Questions

Everything you need to know about CertiFlow

Do my subcontractors or their insurance brokers need to make an account?

No. Subcontractors and brokers will refuse to adopt software that requires yet another login. When you add a subcontractor, CertiFlow sends a secure magic link where they can drag and drop their ACORD 25 and endorsement PDFs in 10 seconds.

Does CertiFlow actually read policy endorsements or just expiration dates?

CertiFlow audits both. Many low-cost tools and spreadsheets only track the expiration date in Box 1. CertiFlow's vision extraction engine reads attached policy pages specifically looking for critical ISO forms like CG 20 10 (Ongoing Operations), CG 20 37 (Completed Operations), and CG 24 04 (Waiver of Subrogation).

What happens when a policy is about to expire?

CertiFlow initiates automated email reminders 30 days and 14 days prior to policy expiration, directed to both the subcontractor and the insurance broker listed on the original certificate. When the broker sends the updated certificate, it is automatically re-audited and archived.

How does this prepare us for our annual commercial insurance audit?

At audit time, your insurance carrier demands proof that all subcontractors working on your projects carried required limits and named you as Additional Insured. CertiFlow generates a complete, 1-click audit binder with time-stamped certificates and endorsements, preventing costly unearned premium penalties.
